data.description:
## Story

As a developer, `tests/scripts/test-cycle-arbiter.sh` runs fixture-corpus replay tests against 6+ canonical arbiter input scenarios, so that the BLOCK/DEFER/DROP ruling logic is verified against known ground-truth inputs and regressions are caught automatically.

## Done Definitions

- [ ] `tests/fixtures/arbiter/` directory contains at minimum 6 JSON fixture files: 2 BLOCK scenarios, 2 DEFER scenarios, 2 DROP scenarios
- [ ] At least one fixture covers a schema-collision scenario (input with both old SUSTAIN/ACCEPT field and new BLOCK/DEFER/DROP field present simultaneously) — arbiter must reject or normalize gracefully
- [ ] `tests/scripts/test-cycle-arbiter.sh` replays each fixture through the arbiter and asserts the expected ruling; test passes when arbiter output matches expected ruling for all fixtures
- [ ] Test script is executable (`chmod +x`) and follows the behavioral testing standard (`plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/behavioral-testing-standard.md`)
- [ ] Tests run in isolation: no network calls, no ticket system writes, no ARTIFACTS_DIR side effects; all external dependencies mocked or stubbed
- [ ] All 6+ tests pass in CI (`validate.sh --ci` or targeted test run)

## Considerations

- [Ordering] Must run after S3 (arbiter schema defined) and S4 (Jaccard/cycle-K dispatch logic complete); fixtures must reflect the final BLOCK/DEFER/DROP schema
- [Fixture design] Each fixture should be self-documenting: include a `_comment` field explaining the expected behavior and why; avoids change-detector pattern
- [Schema-collision fixture] The schema-collision fixture exercises a real ambiguity that arises during the transition period; if the arbiter rejects it, the error message must be actionable
- [Behavioral testing standard] Read `plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/behavioral-testing-standard.md` before writing tests; no implementation-coupled assertions, no existence-only assertions
- [Escalation policy] Escalate when blocked
